expectations.text: B1: Offers a workable path with static images or a video file instead of a webcam
expectations.evidence: "Yes — a webcam is optional for this project. The Python + OpenCV track runs entirely on still images, and every milestone has a camera-free version" — M1 loads images from disk, M2–5 are "pure image processing, no camera involved", M6 accepts "a saved frame sequence" via cv2.warpPerspective or phone photos; plus a "Fully synthetic (zero hardware)" route.

expectations.text: B2: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: a concrete command to run and the expected output/behaviour
expectations.evidence: Final reply ends: "**How to check it:** `python ar-marker-demo/m1_input.py` → prints `reference: (200, 200, 3), scene: (...)` and opens two windows; any key closes them." Earlier: generate marker one-liner with "(expected: `marker.png` exists, a black square with a white square inside)".

expectations.text: B3: Explains using a reference image plus scene images/video frames as input
expectations.evidence: "Milestone 1 (input): load a reference marker image + a scene image from disk instead of grabbing frames"; "generate the marker yourself (draw it with OpenCV), then create 'scene' images by warping it onto photos"; "any phone photo of the printed marker + a few shots of it on a desk"; "Live video is just this pipeline run at 30 fps; the math is identical on one frame."

expectations.text: B4: Stays inside the workspace and does not run any install command (brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install); if tools are needed it asks the learner to install them
expectations.evidence: "SHELL COMMANDS RUN (0)"; only file written is ar-marker-demo/m1_input.py (inside project). Install left to learner: "Then install what's missing (you run this, I don't): pip install opencv-python numpy" and "(you run installs, I don't)".
